feed.title: Combined summary - RFC: Two years of BIP Editing, time for some new faces?

entry.title: Combined summary - RFC: Two years of BIP Editing, time for some new faces?
entry.summary: Over the two-year period from April 2024 to April 2026, the BIP Editors have overseen a notably active phase in the stewardship of the Bitcoin Improvement Proposals repository. Their efforts included processing nearly six hundred pull requests and facilitating the publication of forty-two new BIPs, which collectively signal a period of revitalization for the repository. This productivity was supported by both visible contributions—such as updating documents, revising procedures, and enhancing continuous integration scripts—and less visible work like addressing abandoned submissions and streamlining workflows. The consolidation of these activities has led to an uptick in engagement around Bitcoin protocol development, fostering a collaborative environment for technical innovation. Despite these advances, the majority of the editorial workload fell to just a small subset of the official editors, with only one editor actively managing daily operations at times. This concentration of responsibility highlighted the unsustainable demands placed on individuals, especially during periods when editors were unavailable, resulting in delays for high-quality submissions that awaited thorough review. To remedy this, there is strong advocacy for expanding the editorial team to three committed members who can share the ongoing responsibilities. Such a change is expected to ensure more consistent management, prevent burnout, and maintain the rigorous standards necessary for reviewing complex proposals. Within the Bitcoin community, there is broad consensus that a lean but highly engaged editorial team best serves the needs of the BIPs repository. The proposal for a three-person team is widely supported, balancing efficiency with effective oversight. Community appreciation has been expressed for editors like Murch, whose dedication has been instrumental to the repository’s recent success. Recognition of individual contributions underscores the importance of having skilled and motivated participants in key roles within open-source projects. Interest in joining the editorial team continues to grow. Contributors such as Jaroslav Dlouhy have proactively sought information about the path to becoming an editor, emphasizing the open and participatory ethos of the Bitcoin project. Prospective editors are encouraged to demonstrate their suitability through ongoing engagement with open pull requests and constructive feedback, which not only helps manage current workloads but also provides practical insight into the nature of editorial responsibilities. The qualifications for a BIP Editor are well defined: prior experience with Bitcoin development or protocol design, proficiency in English, and an aptitude for detail-oriented tasks. A minimum commitment of five to ten hours per week is expected, though actual time invested may vary. Editors must monitor repository activity, prompt authors for reviews and updates, and merge pull requests when ready. While certain administrative functions are reserved for editors, much of the review process is open to the broader community, reflecting Bitcoin’s collaborative development model. For those interested in contributing or understanding the workflow, engagement with ongoing pull requests is encouraged and can be facilitated via [this link](https://github.com/bitcoin/bips/pulls?q=is%3Aopen+is%3Apr+-label%3A%22Metadata+Update%22+-label%3ATypo-to-be-collected+-label%3ACI). The ongoing discussions emphasize the necessity of regular participation and shared responsibility among editors to avoid lapses in proposal management. Suggestions include the possibility of editors serving limited terms, such as twelve to twenty-four months, to make commitments more manageable and attract a broader range of contributors. The active involvement of non-editors in reviewing new BIPs has provided some relief but does not fully compensate for the need for dedicated editorial oversight. Sustained community engagement and transparent, merit-based recruitment remain central to the evolution of the BIPs repository and, consequently, to the advancement of the Bitcoin protocol itself.
